title: Population-scale reconstruction of menopause dynamics reveals a physiological cliff at the final menstrual period

summary: 受天文学启发的计算框架从横断面数据重建末次月经锚定轨迹，在两个队列3亿项检验中发现多系统生理断崖。

abstract: Menopause reshapes female physiology, yet current understanding is limited by small longitudinal cohorts that characterize it as a gradual transition. Large-scale biomedical datasets remain underutilized because the final menstrual period (FMP) age is rarely recorded. Here we present a computational framework, inspired by astronomy, that reconstructs FMP-anchored trajectories from cross-sectional data by removing the blurring caused by variation in FMP age across individuals. Applying this to two independent cohorts totaling 300 million laboratory tests revealed a step-like physiological cliff at the FMP including endocrine, skeletal, hepatic, renal and lipid systems. These discontinuities are absent in male individuals, are concordant across populations and appear markedly attenuated by menopausal hormone therapy. Dysregulation began more than a decade before FMP. These findings support a systemic, quantifiable view of menopause and provide a generalizable strategy for recovering hidden biological trajectories applicable to other transitions such as puberty or disease progression. By using a novel computational framework, a cross-sectional analysis on laboratory data from two independent cohorts reveals that the final menstrual period marks an abrupt, multisystem physiological shift, with sex hormone changes beginning more than 10 years before menopause onset.

zh_abstract: 绝经重塑女性生理，但当前理解受到小型纵向队列的限制，这些队列将其描述为一种逐渐过渡。大规模生物医学数据集仍未得到充分利用，因为末次月经（final menstrual period, FMP）年龄很少被记录。在此，我们提出一个受天文学启发的计算框架，通过去除个体间 FMP 年龄差异所造成的模糊，从横断面数据中重建以 FMP 为锚点的轨迹。将其应用于两个独立队列、总计 3 亿次实验室检测，揭示了在 FMP 处存在阶梯式生理断崖，包括内分泌、骨骼、肝脏、肾脏和脂质系统。这些不连续性在男性个体中不存在，在不同人群中一致，并且似乎被绝经激素治疗显著减弱。失调在 FMP 前十余年就开始。这些发现支持一种系统性、可量化的绝经观，并提供了一种可推广的策略，用于恢复隐藏的生物学轨迹，适用于其他转变，如青春期或疾病进展。通过使用一种新颖的计算框架，对来自两个独立队列的实验室数据进行横断面分析，揭示末次月经标志着一种突然的多系统生理转变，性激素变化在绝经开始前超过 10 年就已出现。

abstract: Abstract We created an interpretable end-to-end neural network (ScoreNet) which can be used to develop an easy-to-implement scoring system for risk stratification. We applied it to data from 2711 patients with advanced melanoma across 5 trials that supported new drug approvals and developed a scoring system for overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS). The scoring system was then validated in two separate trials. This score is a weighted summation based on eight baseline features (sum of longest diameter for all target lesions, lactate dehydrogenase, systemic immune inflammation index, hemoglobin, ECOG performance status, liver metastasis, pulse rate, and PD-L1 immunohistochemistry status). Using the score, patients can be classified into low, moderate, or high-risk categories of reduced OS and PFS. Risk stratification was demonstrated for patients treated with PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors, chemotherapy, CTLA-4 inhibitors, BRAF or MEK inhibitors, and their combinations. ScoreNet-based risk stratification can be a new tool for clinical research/practice.

abstract: Clinical prediction models are increasingly deployed to support diagnostic and prognostic decisions, making reproducibility essential for assessing their reliability and generalizability. Analytical code supports independent assessment of these processes, yet its availability in the literature remains limited. This scoping review quantifies current practices in sharing analytical code to inform the development of TRIPOD-Code, a reporting guideline for code availability and reproducibility. Here a large-language-model-assisted pipeline was developed to screen articles citing TRIPOD or TRIPOD+AI, extract repository links and assess retrieved repositories against 14 predefined reproducibility-related features. Among 3,967 articles, 482 (12.2%) included code-sharing statements. Sharing prevalence varied widely by journal and country. Repository assessment showed substantial heterogeneity in reproducibility features. These findings underscore the need for clearer expectations beyond code availability, including documentation, dependency specification and executable structure. Strengthening these practices may improve the usability of clinical prediction model studies and support their deployment in real-world clinical settings.

abstract: One-third of the world’s 70 million people with epilepsy have seizures uncontrolled by medication, and implantable devices are a promising treatment. These devices can detect impending seizures, missed medication and impaired cognition, but, like most medical devices, they cannot share this information with patients in real time. This is a missed opportunity for devices to learn from clinical events and teach patients how their behaviors affect their health. Here we present a device platform that converses with patients to help them manage their epilepsy. The inpatient prototype links scalp and intracranial electroencephalography (EEG) to a secure, large language model-based artificial intelligence (AI) that communicates bidirectionally through a smartphone app. The AI processes biomarkers of sleep, medication, cognition and seizure probability, notifies patients of clinical events and trends, records symptoms and responses, and uses their feedback to retrain its seizure detector, reducing false alarms. We validated this platform in 13 patients who are undergoing video-EEG monitoring for epilepsy (scalp, n = 11; intracranial, n = 2). In a pseudoprospective simulation, seizure detectors improved precision from patient feedback alone, without expert intervention. We propose this system as a scalable, safeguarded platform for medical devices that can rapidly adapt to patient and provider needs across epilepsy and other medical conditions.

title: Model-dependent prompt effects challenge reliable deployment of medical LLMs in traditional Chinese medicine
zh_title: 模型依赖的提示效应挑战中医医疗大模型可靠部署
summary: 在2025年台湾中医师执照考试475题上评测16个LLM与7种提示策略，无提示工程时准确率35.4%–85.9%，约半数通过。
key_points: 评测16个LLM、7种提示策略

abstract: Although contemporary large language models (LLMs) have achieved satisfactory results in Western medical knowledge, their performance on traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) remains underexplored, and the determinants of performance variation are poorly understood. We evaluated 16 LLMs under seven prompt strategies on 475 questions from the 2025 Taiwan national TCM licensing examination, a public benchmark of TCM knowledge. Without prompt engineering, accuracy ranged from 35.4% to 85.9%, with approximately half passing. Among the evaluated model versions, adjusted accuracy differed substantially when models were grouped by family (for example, Claude-family models, 84% vs. GPT-4, 43%); these family-grouped comparisons were descriptive because only 16 individual models were evaluated. Paired prompt analyses showed modest average absolute effects, ranging from a 2.03-percentage-point decrease with implicit CoT to a 3.04-percentage-point increase with explicit CoT. However, prompt–model interactions produced substantial model-level divergence: prompt optimization reversed failing performance in one model (87.4% vs. 49.7%) while reducing accuracy in others. No single prompt strategy yielded consistent benefits across the evaluated models. Among five selected lower-performing models evaluated under explicit CoT prompting, misunderstanding of foundational TCM concepts was the most frequent error. These findings indicate that reliable LLM deployment in TCM requires empirical validation of both model choice and prompt strategy: model selection strongly shapes baseline capability, while prompt-model interactions can materially alter performance.

abstract: Abstract Medical AI requires governance preserving safety during continuous improvement. FDA Predetermined Change Control Plans (PCCP) and EU post-market surveillance address iterative updates but lack operational tooling. We present AEGIS, an internal governance and post-market-monitoring infrastructure designed to support the documentation of predetermined governance pathways for PCCP and Medical Devices Regulation alignment. AEGIS comprises dataset assimilation and retraining, model monitoring, and conditional decision-making modules. It utilizes a four-category taxonomy (APPROVE, CONDITIONAL APPROVAL, CLINICAL REVIEW, REJECT) and an independent ALARM signal. Instantiating AEGIS for sepsis prediction (PhysioNet) and brain-tumor segmentation (BraTS) exercised all decision categories, successfully routing failures to the critical REJECT + ALARM state (no deployable model; released model at risk). On real cross-site data, drift detection ROC-AUC rose from 0.82 to 1.00, reliably triggering near 500-patient batches with zero false alarms. This proof-of-concept utilizes illustrative clinical models; drift scoring quantifies covariate shift only, leaving concept drift for future work.

abstract: Abstract Although continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) provides high-dimensional data, the usefulness of multimodal and diurnal glycemic profiles for disease characterization and risk stratification remains unknown. Here, in the iCanNet cohort of 90,757 participants, we examined the associations of 48 CGM-derived metrics with prediabetes, T2D, and T1D, compared to normoglycemia. We further employed Gaussian Mixture Model to define glycemic phenotypes and established digital glycemic risk score (DGRS) to quantify complication risks in T2D. Participants with prediabetes, T2D, or T1D exhibited distinct CGM signatures compared to normoglycemic individuals (all P < 0.001). Integration of top five metrics significantly improved diabetes classification, and calibration analyses showed agreement between predicted and observed risks. Four glycemic phenotypes were identified in T2D, with sustained hyperglycemia associated with a 59% increased risk of acute complications, and high glycemic variability associated with 75% and 41% higher risks of acute and chronic complications, respectively. The DGRS identified residual risk among patients achieving time in range ≥70%, reclassifying 25.0% and 22.3% of these individuals to high-risk groups for acute and chronic complications, respectively. In summary, this study revealed distinct CGM-derived signatures across diabetes statuses and established a multimodal framework for identifying high-risk individuals with T2D who may be overlooked by conventional biomarkers.

abstract: This study aimed to characterize population-level and individual-level metabolic and radiomics-derived structural brain networks across healthy controls (HC), mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and Alzheimer’s disease (AD) using multimodal PET and MRI. A total of 651 participants with both [ 18 F]FDG PET and MRI were retrospectively included, with an external cohort of 45 participants used for validation. Thirty-two AD-relevant regions of interest were retained as network nodes and characterized using PET standardized uptake value ratios (SUVRs) and a selected MRI radiomics descriptor. Population-level networks were constructed using probability density function-based similarity with Jensen–Shannon divergence, and individualized perturbation networks were derived relative to an HC reference. Network-derived features were evaluated for prediction. Both SUVR-based and radiomics-based networks showed distinct patterns in MCI and AD compared with HC. Fused network features improved discrimination compared with either modality alone, achieving one-vs-rest AUCs of 0.894 [0.868–0.917] for HC, 0.888 [0.862–0.912] for AD, and 0.814 [0.783–0.844] for MCI. These findings indicate graded network disorganization across the HC–MCI–AD spectrum and support multimodal prediction.

abstract: Cancer cachexia is a wasting syndrome with outsized impact on morbidity and mortality, yet its drivers and systemic consequences remain poorly defined. In this study, we repurposed longitudinal clinicogenomic data from 52,236 patients with cancer profiled by MSK-IMPACT (2010–2024) at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center to define episode-resolved trajectories of consensus-defined cachectic weight loss and linked these events to outcomes, serology and tumor genotypes. Cachectic episodes clustered near periods of disease progression and were associated with inferior outcomes in nearly all cancer types. Across diverse malignancies, cachectic weight loss episodes exhibited a consistent serologic signature characterized by lower albumin and hemoglobin and higher levels of liver enzymes. Numerous somatic tumor genotypes, including TP53 mutation across several diseases, were also associated with more frequent onset of cachectic episodes. Motivated by these observations, we developed a multivariate model to predict impending risk of cachectic weight loss in patients with lung, colorectal and prostate cancer, validated in an independent, external cohort from Dana-Farber Cancer Institute (n = 5,785). Routine clinicogenomic data are, therefore, a scalable resource for discovery in cancer cachexia. Using longitudinal data from 52,236 patients with cancer, this study created a multimodal atlas of cancer cachexia, demonstrating that weight loss episodes are linked to systemic serologic signatures and specific tumor genotypes and can be predicted using integrated clinical and molecular data, enabling earlier identification.

abstract: [DEN open] Small bowel capsule endoscopy (CE) produces lengthy videos that are time-consuming to review and susceptible to missed lesions. We evaluated whether an open-source, pretrained artificial intelligence (AI) model (SEE-AI) could improve diagnostic performance and interpretation efficiency compared with conventional reading. We retrospectively analyzed 249 PillCam SB3 examinations performed between 2007 and 2022 at six hospitals, using a two-reader crossover design. SEE-AI (confidence threshold 0.1) generated annotated videos with bounding boxes for eight lesion categories. The primary endpoints were sensitivity for lesion detection on a per-lesion and per-patient basis. Secondary endpoints included specificity, predictive values, overall accuracy, and reading time. A prespecified subgroup analysis evaluated cases of suspected small-bowel bleeding (SSBB), focusing on Saurin P1+P2 hemorrhagic lesions. Across 1550 adjudicated lesions, AI-assisted reading demonstrated higher sensitivity than conventional reading (per-lesion: 98.8% [1532/1550] vs. 86.4% [1339/1550]; per-patient: 99.1% [464/468] vs. 80.3% [376/468]; both p < 0.0001). The mean reading time decreased from 17.9 to 13.7 min (p < 0.0001). In SSBB cases (n = 131), sensitivity for P1+P2 lesions improved on both a per-lesion basis (98.2% [439/447] vs. 82.8% [370/447]) and per-patient basis (98.6% [145/147] vs. 73.5% [108/147]), with a shorter reading time (14.1 vs. 18.0 min; all p < 0.0001). In this multicenter evaluation, SEE-AI significantly improved lesion detection and reduced reading time for CE interpretation, including SSBB cases, while maintaining openness and reproducibility. AI-assisted reading may reduce clinicians' workload and support the adoption of SEE-AI as a practical tool - and a potential future standard of care - for small bowel CE. N/A.

abstract: [Infectious Disease Modelling] Accurate influenza forecasting is essential for public health preparedness, yet many models require future covariates, provide limited interpretability, and degrade under post-pandemic regime shifts. We propose a Stage-Aware Multimodal Neural Network (SAMNN) that integrates multimodal temporal features using configurations adapted to heterogeneous transmission regimes and supports season-ahead scenario forecasting using adversarially synthesized covariates. Using 13 years of national A/H1N1 surveillance data from mainland China (2011∼2024), SAMNN was evaluated across three epidemiologically distinct seasons spanning ∼20-fold differences in peak intensity. SAMNN achieved R 2 values of 0.82-0.95, 0.82-0.97, and 0.55-0.97 for 1-week-, 2-week-, and 4-week-ahead forecasting, respectively, and generally maintained competitive performance relative to five baseline models across forecast horizons. SHAP attribution showed that epidemiological signals dominated predictions, with context-dependent contributions from climatic and social-context features. To support prospective scenario forecasting, we used an adversarial synthetic covariate-generation pipeline to produce season-ahead forecasts for 2024/25 using information available at the prespecified forecast origin.

abstract: [Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry] To develop artificial intelligence (AI)-based intelligent review rules to accurately screen samples that require retests or blood smear microscopy examinations, thereby reducing the review rate, improving the work efficiency of haematology laboratories, and ensuring the quality of whole blood analysis. A total of 10,212 EDTA-K2 venous blood samples from the clinical laboratories of 4 hospitals from May 2022 to April 2025 were collected. Among them, 9000 samples from the First People's Hospital of Foshan, the Zhongda Hospital affiliated to Southeast University, and the First Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-sen University were used to establish the rules, and 1212 samples from the Zhongshan Hospital affiliated to Fudan University were used for rule validation. The obtained rules were compared with the 41 review rules set by the International Consensus Group for Haematology Review (ICGHR). All samples were tested using a haematology analyser under the customized dilution ratio (CDR) mode and smear microscopy, if the microscopic examination results trigger the 10 microscopic anomalous rules established by the ICGHR, then the sample is deemed to be an anomalous sample. Intelligent review rules were established using the gradient boosting decision tree (GBDT) algorithm. Moreover, the false negative rate, false positive rate, and review rate of the validation set were statistically analysed. (1) Among the 9000 samples in the establishment set, 4493 anomalous samples were identified by microscopic examination, and 26 intelligent review rules were established using the GBDT algorithm. (2) For the external validation set, 180 anomalous samples were identified by microscopic examination. Compared with those of the 41 international review rules, the false positive rate (14.60%) and review rate (27.55%) of the intelligent review rules were significantly lower (false positive rate: 30.19%, review rate: 44.14%). The false negative rate of the intelligent review rules (1.89%) was comparable to that of the 41 international review rules (0.90%) and met the ICGHR requirement of a false negative rate < 5%, with no critical hematologic cells missed. Intelligent review rules generated using AI techniques effectively reduce the false positive rate and review rate and prevent missed diagnoses of hematologic cells while ensuring test quality. abstract: Emergency department (ED) crowding is associated with delayed treatment and increased mortality, and proactive staffing requires reliable short-term demand forecasts. Most operational models rely on temporal or weather patterns but may insufficiently capture underlying population vulnerability. We evaluated whether community-level social determinants of health (SDoH) improve the prediction of near-term ED demand compared with weather factors using XGBOOST, and developed an interpretable model to inform resource allocation. The study included 213,138 encounters aggregated into 22,883 hourly observations at a tertiary teaching hospital in Wuhan, China. Neighbourhoods differed markedly in age structure and diagnostic profiles, indicating heterogeneous healthcare needs across the catchment area. Models incorporating dynamic SDoH features consistently outperformed those using weather variables alone. Overall, the composite model achieved the best performance with an RMSE of 3.48 visits per hour, an MAE of 2.62 visits per hour, and an R ² of 0.68. Mean absolute prediction errors were approximately 2 to 3 patients per hour across scenarios, suggesting practical utility for short-term staffing and capacity planning. The study indicates that community-level social vulnerability may provide more informative signals than weather conditions for anticipating short-term ED demand. Integrating SDoH-informed forecasts into hospital operations may enable earlier staffing adjustments and help mitigate crowding-related risks.

abstract: Title and abstract screening is among the most labor-intensive steps of systematic reviews. Jev, a low-cost AI decision model, scores records against eligibility criteria without screening labels. We scored 169,982 records from 128 reviews and, after tuning on development reviews, evaluated 23 held-out reviews once and 31 Cochrane reviews post hoc. Jev outranked the best free ranker in all 23 held-out reviews (mean AUC 0.966 vs 0.831) and came within 0.011 AUC of Claude Opus 5.5 on 1999 records at about 1/700 of its list-price cost (US$0.02/1000 records). Combined with active learning, it raised work saved at 95% recall from 0.659 to 0.806. A fixed score threshold fell below 95% recall in 3 of 28 Cochrane reviews, whereas Jev ranking with statistical stopping (post hoc) reached 95% recall in all 51 reviews, reading 86-88% of records. Label-free ranking with Jev was accurate and inexpensive, but stopping safely required screening decisions.

abstract: [Dialogues in clinical neuroscience] The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into psychiatry is progressing rapidly, with promising yet underexplored applications in suicide prevention. While most existing studies have focused on suicide risk prediction, AI could be applied more broadly across the suicide prevention continuum. This review explores AI's potential in improving the detection of suicidal ideation (SI), enhancing clinician training, and expanding patient access to psychotherapeutic support. Studies suggest that AI models may identify SI more sensitively than clinicians by detecting subtle linguistic or semantic cues. Furthermore, AI-based virtual patients have been shown to improve clinicians' confidence and accuracy in suicide risk assessments, particularly when used alongside traditional training methods. On the patient side, CBT-inspired AI tools offer scalable, on-demand support, but most remain unregulated and clinically unvalidated. Despite their perceived empathy and availability, such tools pose ethical and clinical risks. Many patients use AI tools without professional guidance, a trend clinicians often underestimate. This disconnect calls for urgent regulatory oversight and professional engagement. Without clear clinical validation, AI-based tools may evolve outside medical frameworks, exposing vulnerable individuals to preventable harm. Psychiatry must not only adapt but also lead, ensuring that innovation is harnessed responsibly to serve patients with empathy, safety, and scientific rigor.

title: Realizing the value of the divergence event in clinical human-AI interaction
zh_title: 临床人机交互中「分歧事件」的价值实现
summary: 观点文章提出应从结构、信息、行为三个维度刻画临床AI输出与医生判断不一致时的交互过程。

abstract: When a clinical AI system’s output differs from a human clinician’s judgment, what follows is consequential and underspecified. Current AI interfaces offer only a narrow lane for what happens next: they present the AI output (and its associated potential divergence) as an adjudicative choice for a human to accept, override, or modify. In practice, collapsing this human-AI interaction into a single output inadvertently obscures what happens in a potential divergence event (Fig. 1 ) which can be characterized along three axes: What the workflow and interface allow the clinician to see and do ( structural axis), what information each side brought to the interaction ( informational axis), and how the clinician engaged with the AI’s reasoning rather than only its output ( behavioral axis). When clinical judgment and AI output diverge, clinicians must ultimately decide what to recommend and how to explain their recommendation to the patient, consider their autonomy, accountability, and liability, and bear moral responsibility 1 . A recent systematic review of AI ethics in nursing and midwifery found that AI challenges the role of health professionals not through replacement, but through subtle reconfiguration of the activities that count as care and that emphasis on AI efficiency may risk certain relational aspects of care less visible and valued 2 . Because clinicians often cannot see how an AI system reached its output, they are left to choose between that AI output and their own judgment. Clinicians are told to be the “human in the loop” but are typically given no method for doing so beyond “exercising their judgment” 3 . Efforts to make AI output both more technically explainable and human interpretable - have not directly correlated with improved clinical decisions and have sometimes created false confidence in incorrect AI output 4 .

abstract: Decision models like Jev read text and return probabilities, categories, or ordinal levels, with confidence scores for the latter two, at a fraction of large language models' (LLMs) cost. We explored how Jev could be integrated into clinical workflows for all these output types: mortality risk estimation, categorical Choosing-Wisely decisions for patient questions, and ordinal colon cancer staging. With standard LLM-style inputs, Jev trailed five flagship LLMs: mortality AUROC was 0.822 versus 0.837-0.846; Choosing-Wisely accuracy, 87.7% versus 98.4-100%; and staging accuracy, 45.4% versus 94.2-100%. Developer-recommended input alterations improved staging accuracy to 75.8% with medical context, 82.1% with task decomposition, and 85.8% with both. None of Jev's staging errors had full confidence. Using Jev for fully confident staging decisions and LLMs for the rest was non-inferior to each LLM alone and cut flagship LLM costs by 33-44%. Prompted as designed, decision models may efficiently share structured clinical tasks with LLMs.

This investigation evaluated whether LCI reduces false-positive AI detections compared with white-light imaging (WLI). WLI and LCI were performed sequentially within the same endoscopic session in each patient. LCI assessment performed after WLI observation yielded fewer false-positive CAD-EYE detections while maintaining lesion detection sensitivity. Precise translational control of gene expression is essential for engineering desired traits in this organism, yet the design of functional ribosome binding sites (RBS) in P. denitrificans remains hindered by limited understanding of their sequence-activity relationships. To address this gap, we systematically profiled 1335 native RBS sequences via integrated transcriptomic and proteomic analyses. We found that RBS strength is predominantly governed by a purine-rich Shine-Dalgarno motif located 5-8 bp upstream of the start codon, with specific A/G patterns in this region serving as key determinants. Building on this dataset, we developed and compared CNN, BiLSTM, and Transformer models for RBS strength prediction; among them, the CNN achieved the highest predictive correlation (Pearson r = 0.68). Additionally, a WGAN-GP framework was implemented to generate novel RBS sequences, which were subsequently filtered and evaluated by the prediction framework to enable the design of RBSs with user-specified strengths. Experimental validation showed a relatively strong correlation between predicted and measured strengths (Pearson r = 0.75). This work establishes the first deep learning-enabled RBS design platform for P. denitrificans, offering a robust tool for precise translational regulation and advancing synthetic biology applications in environmental biotechnology.

abstract: [Bioactive materials] Chronic non-healing wounds remain a major clinical challenge, with limited therapeutic efficacy and a huge burden on patients. Nanozymes have emerged as promising bioactive platforms for wound repair by modulating reactive oxygen species, immune responses, angiogenesis, and antimicrobial defense. However, traditional nanozyme development primarily relies on empirical approaches, resulting in limited functional specificity and suboptimal therapeutic outcomes. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have provided promising alternatives to overcome these limitations and accelerate the rational engineering of nanozymes. This review proposes a pathology-informed design framework that links wound-specific therapeutic needs to nanozyme screening, function optimization, and iterative refinement. We synthesize current progress in AI-enabled material discovery and structure-activity prediction, function-oriented and multiobjective optimization, development of stimuli-responsive systems, and elucidation of biological mechanisms. We further examine how these approaches support pathology-guided functional matching, coordination of multifunctional interventions, treatment monitoring, and closed-loop feedback optimization. Key challenges include heterogeneous and biased datasets, limited model generalizability, weak correlation between in vitro catalytic metrics and in vivo efficacy, insufficient wound-relevant endpoints, and incomplete long-term safety assessments. Future work should strengthen the links among material properties, catalytic behavior, and tissue-repair outcomes, while incorporating pathological conditions, delivery systems, and therapeutic feedback into model optimization.

abstract: [Bioactive materials] Organoids, as three-dimensional bioactive microtissues capable of recapitulating native organ architecture and function, have become valuable models in biomedical research. However, their broad adoption is constrained by subjective morphological assessment and endpoint assays that compromise standardization and scalability. This review introduces Organoid Intelligent Morphomics (OIM), an integrative analytical framework that synergizes imaging technologies with artificial intelligence to establish a "morphology-function-mechanism" mapping. OIM enables a paradigm shift from qualitative to quantitative analysis, from static to dynamic monitoring, and from superficial observation to deep molecular inference. The applications of OIM are critically examined across three interconnected domains: (1) quality control, encompassing real-time assessment through non-invasive viability quantification and morphological evaluation, as well as predictive quality control for early differentiation outcome forecasting; (2) disease deconstruction, enabling quantitative, multiscale phenotyping of disease morphology and establishing morphology-mechanism association analyses; (3) drug development, facilitating high-throughput efficacy screening, toxicity assessment, and personalized therapeutic guidance. Furthermore, we critically analyze the current data, algorithmic, and translational challenges facing OIM, propose corresponding solutions, and provide a roadmap toward artificial intelligence virtual organoids. Ultimately, OIM holds promise for establishing the critical technological infrastructure for the scalable manufacturing and clinical translation of organoid-based therapeutics.

abstract: Short-wave infrared hyperspectral imaging (SWIR-HSI) enables rapid, non-destructive material characterization with high potential for process analytical technology and pharmaceutical screening. Here, we demonstrate high-throughput, full-field SWIR-HSI using Fourier transform spectroscopy (FTS) coupled with deep learning. Conventional FTS typically requires thousands of sampling points over a wide optical path difference (OPD) range to resolve spectral features. By directly processing raw interferograms with deep learning, bypassing conventional Fourier transformation, we achieved 98.9% pixel-level and 100% whole-tablet classification accuracy across 11 over-the-counter pharmaceutical products using only 200 data points acquired over a 10 μm mirror displacement (20 μm OPD). Under challenging independent-lot, multi-day testing conditions, the framework maintained 96.7% pixel-level and 100% whole-tablet accuracy. Latent-space visualizations confirmed that short-range interferograms retain sufficient chemical and physical information for rapid, robust pharmaceutical classification. These findings indicate that deep-learned short-range interferometry offers a promising, vibration-resilient approach for high-throughput, non-destructive quality control of solid dosage pharmaceuticals.

We propose a data-efficient ML pipeline for detecting duodenal epithelial neoplasia in whole-slide images. MethodsWe assembled a five-hospital dataset of haematoxylin and eosin-stained duodenal biopsy whole slide images (WSIs) at 10x magnification, comprising 8,027 normal and 401 neoplastic biopsies, including adenomas, carcinomas and neuroendocrine tumours. WSIs were divided into patches and encoded using the Hibou-B foundation model. We compared global standardisation with unsupervised site-specific standardisation of patch embeddings. Our pipeline combined principal component analysis, a Gaussian mixture model and a Random Forest classifier. We assessed generalisability using leave-one-hospital-out cross-validation across four hospitals and on an independent test set from a fifth hospital. ResultsIn leave-one-hospital-out cross-validation, the pipeline achieved a mean accuracy of 90%, sensitivity of 96%, specificity of 83% and an AUC of 0.96. On the external test hospital, it achieved 94% accuracy, 93% sensitivity, 95% specificity, and AUC of 0.97. Site-specific standardisation improved mean cross-validation accuracy by 20 percentage points compared with global standardisation, while the Gaussian mixture pipeline improved accuracy by 12 percentage points compared with mean pooling of patch embeddings. ConclusionsWe present a data-efficient ML approach for detecting duodenal epithelial neoplasia from WSIs. Strong performance was maintained across hospitals and on an independent external test cohort despite the limited number of neoplastic training cases, supporting the feasibility of foundation-model-based approaches for rare histopathological diagnoses.

abstract: Background: Estimating nutrient intake from meal photographs with vision-language models (VLMs) is now practical, but patient photographs often cannot leave the institution. We developed PLANS (Personal-device Local Assessment of Nutrients System), in which a small open VLM runs entirely on a personal device. Methods: Open VLMs were compared on two image sets with reference values (NutriImage, 887 Japanese meals; SNAPMe, 1,134 US meals), and the selected model (Qwen3-VL-4B, 4-bit) was run on an iPad Air without network access. Energy (primary outcome), protein, fat, carbohydrate and salt were evaluated by median absolute percentage error (MedAPE) and Spearman rank correlation (rho). The effect of supplying the food weight, including errors in it, was examined. Results: Energy estimates on the iPad were identical to those of a desktop-computer run for 84-86% of images (other values, 75-87%). MedAPE on the iPad was 37.0% and 36.5% for energy (26-28% of images within +/-20%), 43-65% for the macronutrients and 68-101% for salt (rho 0.51-0.85). On the desktop computer, supplying the true weight reduced MedAPE of the 4B model on NutriImage from 37.0% to 32.5% for energy and from 100.0% to 66.8% for salt; energy MedAPE stayed below the base value for declared weights of 0.5-1.25 times the true weight or rounded to 50 g, but rose markedly when the container weight was included. abstract: Objective Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to generate, summarize, and evaluate clinical documentation, yet standardized methods for evaluating nuanced, context-dependent clinical language remain limited. Existing approaches rely primarily on annotated clinical corpora or keyword-based methods, restricting reproducibility, public dissemination, and systematic comparison across models. Materials and Methods Candidate clinical sentences were generated using a frontier language model and iteratively reviewed according to a clinician-developed annotation rubric refined through expert review in stigmatizing language. The resulting benchmark intentionally incorporates explicit stigmatizing, neutral, and contextually ambiguous ("gray-zone") documentation requiring clinical reasoning rather than keyword recognition. Discussion and Conclusion ClinStigma establishes a reproducible clinician-guided framework for developing synthetic evaluation benchmarks for contextual clinical language. abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have substantially advanced Radiology Report Generation (RRG), yet aligning them through reinforcement learning (RL) remains challenging due to heterogeneous medical supervision. Vanilla Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) assigns uniform credit across the entire generation, leading to segment interference, token dilution, and rationale-diagnosis decoupling, which exacerbates clinical hallucinations. We propose HERO (Hierarchical rationalE Reasoning Optimization), a factorized policy optimization framework that aligns heterogeneous supervision with three optimization granularities. HERO separately optimizes reasoning, diagnosis, and rationale faithfulness through complementary segment-, token-, and completion-level optimization with a heterogeneous reward formulation covering diagnostic accuracy, reasoning quality, and think-answer consistency. Experiments on MIMIC-CXR and IU-Xray show that HERO outperforms strong supervised and reinforcement learning baselines, achieving state-of-the-art clinical efficacy while producing more rationale-supported and think-answer-consistent reports, thereby substantially mitigating clinical hallucinations.

abstract: Background: Patients increasingly consult free artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots about their symptoms, but these models may favour agreement with the patient over accuracy. In obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA), where most cases in the general population remain undiagnosed and diagnosis depends on referral, this could validate symptom denial. We tested whether consumer chatbots maintain guideline-concordant referral when a simulated patient minimises symptoms. Methods: Seven guideline-concordant and standardised OSA vignettes (apnoea-hypopnoea-index, AHI 8-52 events/h; body mass index 28-42 kg/m2) were presented to five free chatbots (GPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Claude Sonnet 4.6, DeepSeek V4 Flash and Grok-4.3) under neutral and symptom-minimising conditions (10 simulated conversations per model-vignette-condition cell; N=700). Referral maintenance was scored by a structured rubric and every capitulation was human-confirmed. Results: All chatbots maintained referral recommendations in neutral conversations (350/350; 100%). When simulated patients minimised symptoms and resisted referral, maintenance fell to 64.3% (225/350), a reduction of 35.7 percentage points (95% CI 5.5-66.0; p=0.028). Rates ranged from 55.7% to 85.7% across chatbots, but evidence of between-chatbot differences was inconsistent across analyses. Rates differed across clinical vignettes (p=0.001). A variance analysis estimated greater variation between vignettes than between chatbots. In the three driving-risk vignettes, referral recommendations were abandoned in 46-68% of symptom-minimising conversations, pooling all five chatbots within each vignette. Conclusions: Consumer AI chatbots abandoned correct OSA referral recommendations in about one-third of symptom-minimising conversations, with higher observed abandonment in simulated cases involving driving risk. This may delay appropriate assessment and raises patient- and public-safety concerns.

abstract: This paper shows that it is possible to predict which newly published biomedical research papers will be connected to subsequent clinical trials. We use CAR-T cell therapy as a proof-of-concept setting because its development can be followed from published research through clinical testing, regulatory approval, and commercialization. We reconstructed connections between research papers and clinical trials and trained machine-learning models to predict which papers were associated with research that progressed to clinical testing. Using 65 paper-inherent indicators, including scientific topic, language, biomedical orientation, and team structure, the models achieved a cross-validated AUC of 0.908. The resulting rankings were also practically informative. In a retrospective analysis using no information generated after 2016, 80% of the top 20 papers came from laboratories associated with one of 13 predefined major CAR-T clinical or commercial outcomes. As an additional finding, first-year citations alone achieved an AUC of 0.797, while provenance indicators based on author, journal, and institutional reputation performed less strongly and added little to the paper-inherent model. Our results show that whether biomedical research papers will be connected to subsequent clinical trials can be predicted from newly published papers with high discrimination in CAR-T. abstract: In response to the success of proprietary Large Language Models (LLMs), there is a growing interest in developing open, non-proprietary LLMs and AI foundation models (AIFMs) for transparent use in academic, scientific, and non-commercial applications. Open models have substantial potential to improve healthcare applications. In this paper, we provide a comprehensive survey and a taxonomy of state-of-the-art open LLMs and AIFMs for clinical tasks. In addition, we empirically evaluate open-weight LLMs on a personalized-prescription task and compare them with a proprietary model with and without Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). Across 100 synthetic patient profiles, the open-weight models matched or exceeded the proprietary baseline on overall suitability accuracy without retrieval augmentation (0.810--0.850 versus 0.780), although the confidence intervals overlap; with retrieval augmentation, every model improved, and the ranking closed to within 0.04. Gains from RAG were field-dependent rather than uniform. To highlight the clinical relevance of LLM-driven personalized prescriptions, we also conduct a subjective evaluation in which two raters, blinded to model and condition, scored responses independently of each other. Their ratings did not follow the accuracy gains: retrieval raised overall suitability accuracy for every model while lowering the two-rater means for two of the four on all five dimensions. Finally, we outline the ethical implications and potential risks associated with the misuse of advanced LLMs and AIFMs, highlighting the importance of responsible and transparent deployment in healthcare contexts. \textit{Data and code used in the paper will be released upon publication.

abstract: Objectives: Patients and clinicians increasingly ask large language models (LLMs) about Kampo, Japan's traditional medicine. Yet evaluations of LLMs have measured accuracy on examination questions, which ask what a model knows; a consultation asks whether it can apply that knowledge to the patient at hand. No benchmark had measured that. Materials and Methods: KampoBench comprises 74 consultation scenarios and 310 conversation-specific rubric criteria, following the design of HealthBench. Scenarios, criteria and reference answers were drafted by an LLM and revised by board-certified Kampo physicians. Ten current models from three vendors were evaluated. Because LLM graders are known to favor their own family, each response was graded by a model from each vendor. Results: The best model reached 74.8-86.3% across graders, the physician-revised reference answers 87.9-92.4%. Rankings were stable across graders (Spearman's rho 0.952-0.976), and the family-favoring deviation was 0.4 to 0.6 percentage points, below the bootstrap standard deviation of one measurement; grader leniency varied by 14.3 points. Models were most reliable on criteria about advising that care be sought (83.6%) and least reliable on those requiring a known crude-drug risk to be tied to the case (17.5%), though 79.2% of those responses named the drug. Discussion: The shortfall lay in applying knowledge to the case rather than in holding it - a distinction examination-format evaluations cannot make. Conclusion: Evaluation in traditional medicine should measure the judgments a consultation requires, not recall alone. Quoted alongside the grader that produced it, a KampoBench score is a usable measure of those judgments.

abstract: Introduction: Horizon scanning in healthcare assesses early signals of innovation, crucial for timely adoption. Current horizon scanning faces challenges in efficient information retrieval and analysis, especially in grey literature, presenting a need for innovative tools. Methodology: This article introduces SCANAR and AIDOC, open-source Python-based tools designed to improve horizon scanning. SCANAR automates the retrieval and processing of news articles, using de-duplication and unsupervised relevancy ranking. AIDOC aids filtration by leveraging large language models and text embeddings for calculation of semantic similarity, to reorder data based on relevancy. Results: Twelve internal datasets from horizon scans and four external benchmarking datasets were used. SCANAR improved retrieval efficiency by automating processes previously dependent on manual labour. AIDOC displayed work-saving potential, achieving around 65% theoretic reduction in manual review efforts at 95% recall or 20% reduction when adding CMH, an existing open-source algorithm to make data-driven decisions on stopping screening early. Comparative analysis with benchmarking data showed AIDOC's performance was similar to existing systematic review automation tools, though performance varied depending on dataset characteristics. Conclusion: The validation indicates that SCANAR and AIDOC show potential to enhance horizon scanning efficiency by streamlining data retrieval and prioritisation. These tools may alleviate methodological limitations and allow broader, swifter horizon scans. Further studies are suggested to optimize these models and to design new workflows and validation processes that integrate large language models.

abstract: Cellular reprogramming, the artificial transformation of one cell type into another, has been attracting increasing research attention due to its therapeutic potential for complex diseases. However, identifying effective reprogramming strategies through classical wet-lab experiments is hindered by lengthy time commitments and high costs. In this study, we explore the use of deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to control Boolean network models of complex biological systems, such as gene regulatory and signalling pathway networks. We formulate a novel control problem for Boolean network models under the asynchronous update mode, specifically in the context of cellular reprogramming. To solve it, we devise GATTACA, a scalable computational framework. To facilitate scalability of our framework, we consider previously introduced concept of a pseudo-attractor and improve the procedure for effective identification of pseudo-attractor states. We then incorporate graph neural networks with graph convolution operations into the artificial neural network approximator of the DRL agent's action-value function. This allows us to leverage the available knowledge on the structure of a biological system and to indirectly, yet effectively, encode the system's modelled dynamics into a latent representation. Experiments on several large-scale, real-world biological networks from the literature demonstrate the scalability and effectiveness of our approach.

abstract: ObjectiveTo develop and evaluate a dynamic model that repeatedly estimates the 30-day risk of a first grade [≥]2 immune-related adverse event (irAE) during immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy. Materials and MethodsAdults initiating ICI therapy during 2015-2022 comprised the development cohort; 2023 initiators formed a nonoverlapping internal temporal evaluation cohort. Every 21 days during the first treatment year, models used available EHR information to predict a first structured phenotype-defined grade [≥]2 irAE during the next 30 days. Evaluation included pooled and within-landmark discrimination, precision-recall performance, calibration, and patient-clustered bootstrap confidence intervals. Feature-state ablations and alternative update schedules examined the contribution of dynamic information. ResultsDevelopment included 1,522 patients and 18,744 evaluable landmarks; temporal evaluation included 526 patients and 6,263 landmarks, of which 184 were positive (2.94%). A complete-state extension achieved AUROC 0.719 and AUPRC 0.073. The 21-day schedule had the highest discrimination among tested cadences. ConclusionLongitudinal EHR updating improved near-term irAE prediction beyond pretreatment characteristics and treatment time. Phenotype adjudication and independent evaluation of calibration, transportability, and clinical utility are needed before implementation.

abstract: Clinical AI deployment rarely reaches the bedside because both workstation integration and governed backend provisioning are challenging. We introduce a workflow that allows rapid and governed access to AI functionalities through a browser interface or API, enabling privacy-compliant data analysis. IaC is a concept in which networks, access rights, and service endpoints are written down as machine-readable files that can be reviewed once and executed identically in any institution. Here, we apply this concept to a clinical use case. The process of deploying a governed, private clinical AI solution using this approach in a tertiary care center took, on average, 310.3 +- 196.6 seconds (n=25, mean +- SD). To further demonstrate the clinical value of this approach, we developed and deployed an LLM-based inconsistency checker, which identifies textual inconsistency in medical documents. When evaluating the tool on a set of 1,347 physician-approved clinical documents, the tool flagged a clinically severe inconsistency in 105 clinical documents (7.8%, approximately 1 in 13). abstract: The subcellular localization of RNAs, including long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), messenger RNAs (mRNAs), microRNAs (miRNAs) and other smaller RNAs, plays a critical role in determining their biological functions. For instance, lncRNAs are predominantly associated with chromatin and act as regulators of gene transcription and chromatin structure, while mRNAs are distributed across the nucleus and cytoplasm, facilitating the transport of genetic information for protein synthesis. Understanding RNA localization sheds light on processes like gene expression regulation with spatial and temporal precision. However, traditional wet lab methods for determining RNA localization, such as in situ hybridization, are often time-consuming, resource-demanding, and costly. To overcome these challenges, computational methods leveraging artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) have emerged as powerful alternatives, enabling large-scale prediction of RNA subcellular localization. This paper provides a comprehensive review of the latest advancements in AI-based approaches for RNA subcellular localization prediction, covering various RNA types and focusing on sequence-based, image-based, and hybrid methodologies that combine both data types. We highlight the potential of these methods to accelerate RNA research, uncover molecular pathways, and guide targeted disease treatments. Furthermore, we critically discuss the challenges in AI/ML approaches for RNA subcellular localization, such as data scarcity and lack of benchmarks, and opportunities to address them. This review aims to serve as a valuable resource for researchers seeking to develop innovative solutions in the field of RNA subcellular localization and beyond.

abstract: BackgroundPassively collected smartphone and wearable data, combined with genomic information, may enable scalable early identification of youth who are at risk for substance use disorder. However, heterogeneous data collected in naturalistic settings limit researcher control over data quality, requiring substantial preprocessing. Data cleaning and feature engineering decisions can meaningfully influence analytic outcomes yet are often minimally described or omitted in published work. ObjectivesWe provide rationales and recommendations for common preprocessing challenges in passive sensing research, including establishing inclusion criteria when "outliers" may reflect true behavioral variability, analyzing differences across smartphone operating systems, handling observations collected outside protocol windows, and engineering features for machine learning applications. MethodsWe illustrate principled approaches to these challenges using smartphone and Fitbit data from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive DevelopmentSM Study (ABCD). The sample was drawn from the available half of the year-4 follow-up (data release 5.1; N = 4,754; ages 13-14). ResultsExtreme outlying observations were concentrated among low-engagement participants with few observed days. Smartphone usage among Apple users appeared under-recorded relative to Android users when compared with self-report measures. Fitbit-derived behavior differed systematically between observations collected within versus outside protocol windows. We also identified potential errors in the studys default preprocessing pipeline. ConclusionWe recommend prioritizing person-level inclusion criteria that preserve meaningful behavioral variability, examining temporal distributions rather than assuming observations are exchangeable, and thoroughly investigating and reporting data quality issues. Although illustrated using the ABCD Study, these principles broadly apply to research using smartphones, wearables, and other digital data sources.

abstract: Environmental exposures shape disease risk, but the generalizability of circulating protein-based readouts of exposures across diverse populations remains unknown. Using plasma proteomic profiles of 5,416 proteins in 10,043 participants from the All of Us Research Program, we evaluated associations with and composite scores of 100+ exposures, spanning adiposity, air pollution, ambient temperature, and substance use. We find that proteomic exposure signatures are largely consistent across populations and socioeconomic strata, with <1% of proteins showing significant cross-population heterogeneity, which included BMI as an exception, with leptin being the most heterogeneous association. Population-specific leptin trajectories adiposity, together with residual leptin-type 2 diabetes associations after BMI adjustment, revealed sex-specific metabolic risk not captured by BMI alone. Aggregated protein scores were largely exposure-specific, but substance-use scores showed cross-prediction and SES scores were broadly associated. PM2.5 protein scores captured within-region exposure variation and outperformed geographic and socioeconomic correlates, but spatial confounders remain embedded within protein-environment associations. Scores trained in UK Biobank transferred to All of Us for biologically proximal exposures, supporting cross-biobank portability. These findings establish plasma proteomics as a scalable framework for exposure measurement across diverse populations, while underscoring that responsible applications require careful consideration of biological context, social patterning, and cohort structure.

abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) preprocessing determines signal quality and interpretation, particularly for transcranial magnetic stimulation combined with EEG (TMS-EEG), where recordings are affected by large and complex stimulation-related artifacts. Several preprocessing approaches have been developed, but substantial variability remains in how pipelines are implemented, documented, and evaluated across recordings, limiting reproducibility and comparability across studies. We developed NESTApp, a MATLAB-based graphical interface built on EEGLAB, to provide an accessible and reproducible framework for implementing and evaluating TMS-EEG preprocessing pipelines. Rather than prescribing a specific pipeline, NESTApp allows users to construct and consistently apply customisable workflows incorporating established EEGLAB and TMS-EEG processing tools, while automatically documenting processing decisions and parameters. Integrated quality-control procedures track data removal and flag recordings based on user-defined criteria, facilitating systematic evaluation across participants. The application also supports group-level visualisation and export of processed TMS-EEG measures for subsequent analyses. Applied to 29 recordings from 16 participants, NESTApp processed 27 and identified those requiring further inspection. By integrating pipeline implementation, documentation, quality control, and group-level evaluation within a single interface, NESTApp provides a transparent framework for TMS-EEG preprocessing that may improve reproducibility, facilitate consistent processing across cohorts, and lower technical barriers to the implementation of established preprocessing approaches.

abstract: BackgroundElectronic health records (EHRs) are central to NHS clinical practice, and the value of the data they hold depends on clinicians entering structured data. Structured data entry (SDE) is nonetheless used inconsistently, and most evidence comes from US settings documenting barriers rather than the mechanisms interventions must target. This is, to our knowledge, the first study to apply the Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB) to SDE, to examine SDE behaviour among UK NHS doctors, and to apply corpus linguistics to clinicians free-text accounts of EHR use. MethodsA two-part mixed-methods study was conducted at a large NHS teaching hospital in central London using the Epic EHR. Study 1 was a cross-sectional survey of non-consultant grade doctors comprising the System Usability Scale (SUS), a purpose-designed TPB questionnaire, and two open-text questions analysed using corpus linguistics. Study 2 was an Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis (IPA) of semi-structured interviews with six resident doctors. ResultsEighty-three doctors responded; 65 completed the SUS and 49 the TPB questionnaire. Mean SUS score was 62.1 (95% CI 58.3-65.9), below the benchmark of 68 and equivalent to a grade of "D". Structured features were used markedly less often than narrative notes. TPB constructs explained 56% of the variance in intention (F(3,45) = 18.95, p < .001); attitudes (p = .003) and subjective norms (p = .009) predicted intention independently, whereas perceived behavioural control did not (p = .14). Intention predicted self-reported use of problem lists, event-specific templates and standardised documents, but not narrative notes. Corpus analysis identified time pressure and interface friction as dominant barriers. IPA generated four themes: structured documentation as cognitive relief; as fragile collective infrastructure; as a practice clinicians are expected to perform but not enabled to learn; and as a format that can flatten clinical reasoning. ConclusionsEngagement with SDE is driven principally by attitudes and social norms rather than by perceived control, and the barriers clinicians describe arise from the intersection of interface design, training, team norms and institutional expectation. Interventions addressing usability alone are unlikely to succeed: sustained change requires team-level normative reinforcement, specialty-relevant training that explains both how and why, and systems that preserve space for clinical narrative.

zh_abstract: 【背景】电子健康记录（EHR）是NHS临床实践的核心，其所含数据的价值取决于临床医生录入结构化数据。尽管如此，结构化数据录入（SDE）的使用仍不一致，且大多数证据来自美国环境，记录的是障碍而非干预必须针对的机制。据我们所知，这是首个将计划行为理论（TPB）应用于SDE、考察英国NHS医生SDE行为，并将语料库语言学应用于临床医生关于EHR使用的自由文本叙述的研究。【方法】在伦敦市中心一家使用Epic EHR的大型NHS教学医院开展了一项由两部分组成的混合方法研究。研究1是对非顾问级别医生进行的横断面调查，包括系统可用性量表（SUS）、专门设计的TPB问卷，以及两个使用语料库语言学分析的开放文本问题。研究2是对六名住院医生半结构化访谈进行的解释现象学分析（IPA）。【结果】83名医生作出回应；65名完成了SUS，49名完成了TPB问卷。平均SUS得分为62.1（95% CI 58.3–65.9），低于68的基准，相当于“D”级。结构化功能的使用频率明显低于叙述性记录。TPB构念解释了意向方差的56%（F(3,45) = 18.95，p < .001）；态度（p = .003）和主观规范（p = .009）独立预测意向，而感知行为控制则没有（p = .14）。意向预测了自我报告的问题列表、事件特定模板和标准化文档的使用，但不能预测叙述性记录的使用。语料库分析确定时间压力和界面摩擦是主要障碍。IPA产生了四个主题：结构化记录作为认知缓解；作为脆弱的集体基础设施；作为一种临床医生被期望执行但未被赋能学习的实践；以及作为一种可能压平临床推理的格式。【结论】对SDE的参与主要由态度和社会规范而非感知控制驱动，临床医生描述的障碍源于界面设计、培训、团队规范和机构期望的交叉。仅解决可用性的干预不太可能成功：持续改变需要团队层面的规范强化、解释如何做以及为何做的专科相关培训，以及为临床叙事保留空间的系统。
